title: Controls drawn over page buttons, a fieldset of checkboxes, a menubar and a file input
blurb: Four more controls from the ui-feed collection, rebuilt around native elements: a pagination marker that stretches from page to page, a road sign whose route avoids what you check, a menubar over a workshop ledger, and a T-shirt that a PNG is printed onto.
question: Can a marker that slides over native buttons draw the text it covers in another colour, with no second copy of the text?
result: Yes: the canvas draws the element twice, the second time clipped to the marker with a CSS filter on the context that turns the ink white or paper coloured. The pagination, the toggle keys and the menubar all use it, and the hit regions stay on the native elements. All four took taps and keys on an emulated phone and stopped painting at rest. Nothing here is verified on a phone.
